observations: Photo 0 shows the motorcycle instrument cluster with two analog gauges, handlebars, ignition key, and Jiji/Osisiogu Library watermarks.
Photo 1 shows a black fuel tank with "Kawasaki" lettering visible on the side, a worn black seat, and scuffed bodywork.
Photo 2 shows the rear wheel with a red-rim stripe, disc brake, chain, sprocket, and an exhaust muffler with visible discoloration/rust at the tip.
No model badge or "ZZR" marking is visible in any of the three photos.

claims.evidence: Kawasaki is readable on the tank in photo 1, but ZZR is not visible in any photo.
Photos are static; no running condition is shown.
No purchase documents or receipts are visible.
Brake disc is visible in photo 2, but gear and brake function cannot be tested from photos.
Photo 2 shows rust/discoloration on the exhaust tip.
No documentation or part numbers are visible to confirm originality.

risks.risk: The claimed ZZR model may be wrong or absent; a different Kawasaki model would change the price.
risks.proof: Clear close-up of the model badge or registration document showing the exact model and chassis/engine numbers.
risks.if_unproven: price as an unidentified Kawasaki motorcycle at the lowest variant value.

risks.risk: Engine or gearbox may not work despite the seller's claim.
risks.proof: Video of a cold start, idle, throttle response, and gear shifting.

risks.risk: Accident or frame damage may be hidden from the angles shown.
risks.proof: Full walkaround video including the VIN, frame, and both sides of the bike.

risks.risk: Ownership or registration papers may be missing.
risks.proof: Photo of the original vehicle documents.

proof_requests: Close-up of the model badge or registration document showing the exact Kawasaki model and chassis/engine numbers.
Video of the engine starting, running, and the rider operating gears and brakes.
response.reason: The specific Kawasaki model is not readable in the photos, and the model drives the price, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without it.
